_doc: Ahmedabad (AMC) upstream sources for Headwaters. Every artifact Ahmedabad ships names its upstreams here by id, with the artifact in dependsOn.
Gujarat-wide upstreams shared with Surat (IN-GRES, CPCB NWMP) stay under their existing ids in surat.json; Ahmedabad's paths are added to their dependsOn rather than duplicating an id.

sources.publisher: National Water Informatics Centre (NWIC), Ministry of Jal Shakti
sources.license: Government of India open data portal: its copyright policy permits reproduction free of charge in any format without specific permission, reproduced accurately and with the source prominently acknowledged; cited with attribution
sources.notes: Gujarat groundwater-level telemetry on the CKAN portal: Gujarat Surface Water and Ground Water Department six-hourly resources 8e630b14-b563-40c8-905f-b0ce28975a90 (2021-2025) and 9f8ca997-e764-4503-9253-872a2d692aec (2026-2030), and CGWB telemetry 6ea9ef6b-8a90-47d0-bd12-ac90272a2650 and b496e769-a678-4948-bd91-de3894fb9471. The 2021-2025 state resource is row-for-row the 1.1 GB export in the research drop. TRAPS: District tags follow old lines (stations tagged Ahmedabad stand in Botad; stations tagged Gandhinagar, Surendranagar and Sabarkantha stand in Ahmedabad's talukas), so stations are placed by coordinates; names repeat across districts; -1.0 is a placeholder alongside 0.0 and 1.0; telemetry is negative below ground and some stations flip sign mid-series. The portal opens a new resource for each five-year block, so the 2031 resource will need adding.

sources.license: IMD data policy; gridded rainfall retrieved programmatically via imdlib, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Grid cell 23.0 N / 72.5 E, the 0.25-degree intersection nearest the city centre and inside the AMC ward extent. Checked against IMD's own Ahmedabad observatory normal of 783.6 mm (Climatological Table 1991-2020, station index 42647, city.imd.gov.in/citywx/extreme/climate.php?id=42647): this cell returns 800.4 mm over 1991-2020 (+2.1%). The cell east of it, 23.0/72.75, returns 868.3 mm (+10.8%). rainfall-recent-ahmedabad.json must use the same grid point.

sources.publisher: Narmada, Water Resources, Water Supply and Kalpsar Department, Government of Gujarat
sources.license: Gujarat government publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/scrape_gujarat_wrd_dams.py --city ahmedabad --out public/data/ahmedabad-dam-storage.json --supabase (daily, local scheduled job at 12:00 IST, then --backfill-from 7 days back to fill gaps; the host does not answer GitHub runners); --backfill-from 2019-06-07 run once for history on 2026-10-15
sources.notes: Reservoir Data Management System (NIC). One PDF per day at downloads/home_pdf.php?dt=<base64 YYYY-MM-DD>; the index page lists every date from 2019-06-01 and the first non-empty report is 2019-06-07. Reports are frozen as generated (a re-fetch is byte-identical), so the archive is the history. TRAPS: a missing date returns HTTP 200 with ZERO bytes, not an error; row order changes between years (key on dam name); 2019-20 reports lack the SchemeId, LocId and Taluka columns and print the region as a word; the major-schemes table on page 3 is in FEET while the dam statement is in metres; words wrap across lines (WARNI / NG); design capacities are revised over time (Hathmati 145.90 to 152.83 MCM), so the design value is stored per report; Mazum is printed Mazam. Sardar Sarovar is printed in its own block with the Narmada Main Canal discharge at the head regulator (Flow @ HR). Reachable from a non-India datacenter on 2026-10-14. The SSNNL homepage shows today's Sardar Sarovar level in HTML spans but keeps no archive; the CWC weekly bulletin listing has been frozen at 08-05-2025 and uses different live capacities (Kadana 1.472 BCM vs the state's 1,191.7 MCM), so the two must never be mixed.

sources.license: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: AMC's City Map app, linked from 'Know Your Ward' on ahmedabadcity.gov.in. The ward layer is a GeoJSON literal (name Ward_Boundary) inside the app's minified JS bundle; there is no WMS, WFS or REST ward service. 48 wards in 7 zones, matching the SEC final delimitation of 03-10-2020 including the areas added on 18-06-2020 (Bopal, Ghuma, Kathwada). The page hash moves whenever the app is rebuilt, which is also when the bundle filename changes. TWO ATTRIBUTE FAULTS: area_ha holds the km2 value, and Navrangpura's area_sq_km is copied from Jodhpur; the producer recomputes areas from geometry. The same app serves lake points only through an encrypted API; those are not read. The OpenCity 'Amdavad Municipal Corporation Wards Map 2024' KML predates the 2020 extension and is not used.

sources.license: Gujarat government publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual transcription into neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_ahmedabad_wards.py POPULATION, checked against the order's printed total
sources.notes: Final delimitation order of 03-10-2020: 48 wards, 192 councillors; scanned Gujarati, 34 pages. Schedule 2 (pp.33-34) gives each ward's Census 2011 population, total 56,64,062, average 1,18,001, allowed band 1,06,201 to 1,29,801. The SEC's 2026 polls table (corparation-2026.pdf) uses the same 48 wards and 192 seats; no later delimitation found. Ward 33 is Sarkhej in the order where LGD names it Vejalpur.

sources.license: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: neer-vazhvu-api/scripts/build_ahmedabad_supply.py --verify <new budget PDF> after updating FIGURES and their pages
sources.notes: The annual budget is AMC's only current statement of its water sources, treatment plants, STPs and lake programme. 2026-27 is FileRepository,2583 (Gujarati Unicode, raw-water table on printed pp.63-64 = PDF pp.113-114); 2023-24 English is FileRepository,2203. FOUR editions (2020-21 and 2021-22 Gujarati, 2024-25, 2025-26) use a legacy non-Unicode Gujarati font that pdftotext cannot read as digits. The AMC Water Project web page (StaticPage/water_project) has carried the same 2,100 / 1,535 MLD table since early 2022 and is NOT current. Tables carry derived columns: use equals capacity on several rows, and sewage generation is 80% of supply.

sources.publisher: Sabarmati River Front Development Corporation Ltd
sources.license: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation company publication (SRFDCL, wholly owned by AMC), cited with attribution
sources.notes: Undated pages. Environmental improvement: the Vasna barrage retains water for 15 km upstream, and the Narmada canal, which crosses the river a few kilometres upstream of the city, 'makes it possible to replenish the barrage-retained water'; interceptor sewers on both banks take sewage from 38 discharge points. FAQ: the retained water is 'almost continuously discharged for irrigation into the Fatehwadi irrigation canal' and 'periodically recharged from the Narmada Canal'.

sources.license: Gujarat High Court judicial record (Government of India judiciary), cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual: read new orders in R/WP(PIL) 98/2021 (as annexed to NGT filings or mirrored on Indian Kanoon) and add dated status entries
sources.notes: Suo Motu v. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and others, R/WP(PIL) 98/2021, on pollution of the Sabarmati; taken up 06-08-2021; Joint Task Force formed 14-09-2021 under CPCB. The court's case-status site sits behind a captcha and is not machine-watchable, so this is a review cadence, not a detector. Orders reach the public record annexed to later NGT filings (OA 91/2023 WZ) and on Indian Kanoon.

sources.publisher: National Green Tribunal (filings by the Government of Gujarat, GPCB and AMC)
sources.license: Government of India tribunal record, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual: read new affidavits in OA 606/2018 (state compliance) and OA 91/2023 WZ (Sabarmati textile units) and update dated statuses
sources.notes: OA 606/2018 carries the state's periodic sewage and STP compliance affidavits; its March 2026 Part-II Annex I gives Ahmedabad's generation as 'Calculated as per 80% of Water Supply' and treated equal to it (a zero gap by method) and reuse at 26%. OA 91/2023 (WZ) carries AMC's reply annexing Gujarat High Court orders of 07-02-2025, 02-05-2025 and 08-08-2025 with STP completion dates. Also OA 79/2025 (WZ), taken up by the Tribunal on a 9 June 2025 news report on Ahmedabad's vanished water bodies (order of 12-11-2025 added UD&UHD and AMC as respondents; next date 22-01-2026).

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (AMRUT 2.0)
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: As-on status PDFs for AMRUT 2.0 water-supply projects; row 182 of the 02.03.2026 list is AMC's 400 MLD Kotarpur WTP (contract awarded, Rs 138.00 crore, 16-10-2026). The portal's own AMC project list (live HTML) disagrees with AMC's budget on several items (Bhadaj and Okaf lakes, the Expressway-Kamod trunk main).

sources.publisher: Chief Minister's Office, Government of Gujarat
sources.license: Gujarat government publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Government press releases used for dated status: Kharicut phase 1 at 80% (11-03-2025) and the riverfront's three phases by end-2027 (06-06-2026). A release with no figures (the 29-04-2025 Chandola review) is not used for any number.

sources.publisher: Urban Development and Urban Housing Department, Government of Gujarat
sources.license: Gujarat government publication, cited with attribution
sources.notes: Policy for Reuse of Treated Waste Water, 28 May 2018, signed by the Principal Secretary. Not found on any gujarat.gov.in host; the FAOLEX mirror is a scan of the signed policy. Objectives (p.7): 25% of freshwater use from treated wastewater, 70% of treated wastewater reused by 2025, 100% by 2030; thermal plants within 50 km must use it (p.11).

sources.license: Gujarat High Court judicial record (Government of India judiciary), cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual: new lake-encroachment orders via Indian Kanoon (the court's own case status is captcha-gated)
sources.notes: Orders on Ahmedabad's lakes: Shailesh R. Shah (2002) 3 GLR 447 (Chandola tank 121 ha, command 525 ha; ordered water bodies to be gazette-notified); R/SCA 6119/2025 (29-04-2025, stay refused: 'Chandola Lake is a water body and on a water body, no construction can be permitted'; disposed 24-07-2025) and R/SCA 6716/2025 (06-05-2025, stay rejected); Kamal Talav (SCA 15965/2025) and Isanpur (SCA 14892/2025, LPA 1280/2025) dismissed. Indian Kanoon is a mirror; cite the court and case number.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti (first Water Bodies Census, reference year 2017-18)
sources.license: Government of India publication, cited with attribution
sources.refreshMethod: manual; watch for the second census's Gujarat tables
sources.notes: District tables GJ_6MIC_WBS<N>.xls. Ahmedabad district: 1,964 water bodies (ponds 417, tanks 1,369, reservoirs 40, water conservation schemes 138); 176 urban across 10 towns and 67 wards; 63 not in use (all urban); 19 encroached (all urban). Gujarat: 54,069, of which 22 encroached - 19 of them in Ahmedabad. The urban count of 176 equals AMC's own 2026-27 lake count; whether they are the same set is not shown by either source.
